instruction: What does restart-stack.ps1 do in the Arc stack?
output: It is a launcher in launchers/: device-pinned to the Arc, run from an interactive session (session 1). Session-0 services silently fall back to CPU, so scheduled tasks use LogonType Interactive. Paths/commands are from the public repo (README.md, install.ps1, launchers/).

instruction: Why must restart-stack.ps1 run in an interactive session?
output: GPU compute only works in an interactive session (session 1), not a session-0 service — otherwise it silently falls back to CPU. The scheduled tasks use LogonType Interactive for this reason. Paths/commands are from the public repo (README.md, install.ps1, launchers/).

instruction: After editing a config, which script restarts the stack and how do you verify it?
output: Run launchers/restart-stack.ps1, then verify with curl http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{{"model":"local-chat","messages":[{{"role":"user","content":"hi"}}]}}'. Paths/commands are from the public repo (README.md, install.ps1, launchers/).

instruction: What is the one-line install that sets up the stack restart-stack.ps1 belongs to?
output: iex "& { $(irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dirtysouthalpha/intel-arc-llm-stack/main/install.ps1) } -Root C:\arc-llm — installs IPEX-LLM SYCL + mainline Vulkan llama.cpp + llama-swap engines, a default Gemma 3 model, the LiteLLM gateway, autostart tasks, and a firewall rule; it prints your endpoint + API key. Paths/commands are from the public repo (README.md, install.ps1, launchers/).

instruction: Size the context window for gemma3-12b with vram-budget.
output:
python vram-budget/vram_budget.py gemma3-12b --weights 6.8 --kv f16
# The calculator accounts for weights (6.8 GB) + f16 KV cache (sliding-window aware). Use its max num_ctx before picking a llama-swap entry; do not guess.

instruction: Why f16 KV and not quantized KV for gemma3-12b on this stack?
input: gemma3-12b on the IPEX SYCL build (b20250729).
output: Quantized KV (-ctk/-ctv q8_0) crashes this build the same way flash-attn does (GGML_ASSERT in ggml-cpu/ops.cpp). Use f16 KV, no flash-attn, and a small -ub at large ctx.

instruction: Write the llama-swap entry for gemma3-12b at a safe context.
input: gemma3-12b, Q4_K_M, Arc B60 24GB, IPEX SYCL llama-server.
output:
"gemma3-12b":
  cmd: >
    V:\AI\llama-cpp\llama-server.exe -m V:\AI\models\gemma3-12b-Q4_K_M.gguf -ngl 999 --host 127.0.0.1 --port ${PORT} -c 32768 -ub 64 -b 256 -np 1 --no-mmap
  ttl: 1800
# -ngl 999 puts all layers on GPU; -ub 64 keeps the compute buffer small at large ctx; --no-mmap as in llama-swap/models.yaml.

instruction: What breaks if you add -fa to the gemma3-12b llama-server command?
input: gemma3-12b on IPEX-LLM llama-server, SYCL build b20250729.
output: Flash attention is broken in this build: -fa falls back to a CPU op and crashes at warmup (GGML_ASSERT(nbv0 == ggml_type_size(v->type))). Keep FA off; the mainline Vulkan binary does support flash-attention for newer archs.

instruction: Why f16 KV and not quantized KV for qwen3-30b on this stack?

instruction: Write the llama-swap entry for qwen3-30b at a safe context.

    V:\AI\llama-cpp\llama-server.exe -m V:\AI\models\qwen3-30b-Q4_K_M.gguf -ngl 999 --host 127.0.0.1 --port ${PORT} -c 32768 -ub 64 -b 256 -np 1 --no-mmap

instruction: Write the LiteLLM gateway entry that maps alias local-chat to its backend.
output:

  litellm_params:
    model: openai/gemma3-12b-vision
    api_base: http://127.0.0.1:9090/v1

instruction: Why does the gateway entry for local-chat use api_key "swap"?
output: llama-swap (:9090) is the local backend; "swap" is the placeholder key the gateway sends it. Real secrets live in environment variables (os.environ/...) — never literal keys in YAML. LiteLLM YAML must be ASCII only (Windows cp1252 codec).

instruction: Add a builtin Sentinel command as markdown.
input: .sentinel/commands/ — drop a .md file in and it is picked up automatically; builtins ship in dist/builtin on build.
output: Create .sentinel/commands/my-command.md with frontmatter + prompt body, run npm run build (scripts/copy-builtins.cjs copies builtins), and verify with /my-command in the TUI.

instruction: Register an MCP server in sentinel.json.
output: Add the mcp block to sentinel.json; its tools appear as mcp__everything__<tool>. `sentinel mcp` lists discovered tools (stdio + Streamable HTTP).

instruction: Use getInstance() instead of new for a Sentinel manager.
input: Singletons via the exported instance / getInstance() — never `new` the managers.
output: Replace `new Manager()` with `getManagerInstance()` (the exported instance). Direct construction breaks the shared state every other module relies on.

instruction: Fix a Tauri v2 desktop build step.
input: cd gui && npm install && npm run tauri dev — needs a Rust toolchain; artifacts in gui/src-tauri/target/release/.
output: Install Rust (https://rustup.rs), then cd gui && npm install && npm run tauri dev. `sentinel gui` alone runs the GUI in the browser; Tauri gives a real window.

instruction: Write the Sentinel router JSON for a gsd agent rule.
input: router.rules: match agent gsd -> anthropic/claude-sonnet, fallbacks [zai/glm-4.6].
output: {"router": {"default": "zai/glm-4.6", "rules": [{"match": {"agent": "gsd"}, "use": "anthropic/claude-sonnet", "fallbacks": ["zai/glm-4.6"]}], "retry": {"maxAttempts": 2, "baseDelayMs": 200, "maxDelayMs": 2000, "retryOn": [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]}}}

instruction: Explain drop_params in the LiteLLM gateway.
output: drop_params: true tells LiteLLM to drop parameters the local backend does not support instead of erroring, so one client can talk to local and paid models. default_fallbacks [local-chat] routes failures to the free local model.

instruction: Add a TokenRonin provider with health checks.
input: providers: name, base_url, api_key (${ENV}), models; health loop 30s, breaker threshold/cooldown.
output: Add the provider under `providers` with base_url, api_key: ${PROVIDER_API_KEY}, and models. The 30s health loop and failure breaker (threshold/cooldown_seconds) handle failover; provider-excluding retry avoids the dead provider.

instruction: Implement TokenRonin exact-match response caching.
input: features.cache: exact-match response cache; opt-in semantic cache via TR_SEMANTIC_CACHE / TR_SEMANTIC_THRESHOLD.
output: Enable the exact-match cache in features; the semantic cache is opt-in with an HTTP embedder and a similarity threshold. Inspect with GET /v1/cache/stats, clear with DELETE /v1/cache.

instruction: Write a Go test for the TokenRonin spend guard.
input: features.spend_guard: fleet + per-workspace daily caps; tripped cap drops cloud providers.
output: Table-test the guard: under cap -> cloud allowed; fleet cap tripped -> cloud dropped, local served; workspace cap tripped -> same for that workspace. Flat-rate subscriptions meter at zero.

instruction: Fix a YAML file that LiteLLM rejects on Windows.
input: gateway/config.yaml must be ASCII only; LiteLLM reads it with the Windows cp1252 codec.
output: Remove/replace the non-ASCII character, save as ASCII, and redeploy with SCP (not inline base64-over-SSH, which truncates >~2KB).

instruction: Explain why mainline GGUFs are required on this stack.
input: Use mainline GGUFs (ggml-org/unsloth) — ollama's GGUFs fail to load in the IPEX build (gemma3.attention.layer_norm_rms_epsilon missing).
output: Ollama GGUFs lack fields the IPEX build expects, so they fail to load. Use mainline ggml-org/unsloth/bartowski GGUFs.

instruction: Why does gpt-oss-20b use the Vulkan binary?
input: gpt-oss-20b: mainline Vulkan binary, drop -fa; Qwen3-VL: add -fit off.
output: Newer archs (gpt-oss, Qwen3-VL, Omni) run on the mainline Vulkan binary, which enumerates only the Arc and supports flash-attention. gpt-oss needs -fa dropped; Qwen3-VL needs -fit off.

instruction: Write a curl to test the gateway after a restart.
output: curl http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"local-chat","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' — expect a chat-completion JSON reply from the resident model.

instruction: Explain the TokenRonin escalation router.
input: TR_ESCALATION=1 enables the escalation router; detects degenerate output and re-runs on a different provider (sets X-Escalated).
output: With TR_ESCALATION=1, degenerate output triggers a re-run on a different provider and the response carries X-Escalated. It is opt-in.

instruction: Add a TokenRonin webhook subscription.
input: POST /v1/webhooks; HMAC-SHA256 signed deliveries (sha256=<hex>), https only, private/loopback/.local rejected, mandatory secret.
output: Create the subscription with an https URL and a secret; deliveries are HMAC-SHA256 signed. SSRF-guarded: private/loopback/.local targets are rejected.

instruction: Explain TokenRonin multi-tenancy auth.
input: Organizations, workspaces, projects, API keys, users; auth with httpOnly session cookies (no localStorage tokens).
output: Tenancy is org -> workspace -> project, with API keys per workspace and members per workspace. Auth uses httpOnly session cookies; tokens are never stored in localStorage.

instruction: How do you check TokenRonin analytics?
output: Use /stats and /analytics for cost/usage, /history (pagination cap 1000) for requests, /metrics for Prometheus, and /events/stream for live dashboard events.

instruction: Fix a Sentinel patch tool call that traverses outside the repo.
input: Tool layer hardened against path traversal (file/patch), shell injection (search/git), SSRF (web) — see CODE-REVIEW.md.
output: Reject any patch path that escapes the workspace root (resolve + prefix-check), and refuse absolute paths outside the project. The guard is in the tool layer, not the prompt.

instruction: Explain Sentinel auto-compacting context.
input: Long conversations are summarized automatically so you don't hit the wall mid-task.
output: When context grows long, Sentinel summarizes the conversation automatically and continues from the summary, so a long task does not hit the context wall mid-run.

instruction: Write the command to run Sentinel as an MCP server.
input: node dist/cli.js mcp-serve — exposes Sentinel's tools over stdio to any MCP client.
output: node dist/cli.js mcp-serve — point Claude Desktop (or any MCP client) at it over stdio. `sentinel mcp` lists tools when consuming other servers.

instruction: How was gemma3-12b verified on the B60, and what would you re-check after a driver update?
output: Re-run the bench in bench/ (throughput + long-context needle test) in an interactive session and compare with bench/results.md. Gemma 3 12B: 33.6 tok/s gen, pp512 84 tok/s, needle@16K PASS; re-check after any driver/oneAPI change.

instruction: What context and ubatch do you use for gemma3-12b at 32K, and why?
input: gemma3-12b, 32K ctx, IPEX SYCL, f16 KV, no FA.
output: Use -c 32768 with a small -ub (64) and -b 256: the attention compute buffer scales with ubatch x ctx, so a large -ub alloc-fails at long ctx. f16 KV, no flash-attn, no KV-quant on this build.

instruction: How is ANTHROPIC_API_KEY used, and where must its value never appear?
input: Environment variable ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in TokenRonin / LiteLLM config.
output: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is referenced by name from YAML as ${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY} (TokenRonin) or os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (LiteLLM) and substituted at load time. Its literal value must never appear in YAML, chat, logs, or a pasted config snippet — reference it by name only.

instruction: Write a config line that references ANTHROPIC_API_KEY correctly.
output: api_key: ${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}  # TokenRonin style, or os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in LiteLLM gateway/config.yaml. Never a literal value.

instruction: Route a request for alias local-chat through the stack.
input: Client -> LiteLLM :4000 model local-chat -> llama-swap :9090 model gemma3-12b-vision.
output: Client calls :4000 with model "local-chat". LiteLLM maps it to openai/gemma3-12b-vision at http://127.0.0.1:9090/v1. llama-swap loads gemma3-12b-vision on demand (only one big model fits in 24GB), serves it, and unloads after ttl.

instruction: How do you switch the resident model to gemma3-12b-vision?
output: Send a request naming gemma3-12b-vision (via its LiteLLM alias) to :4000; llama-swap hot-swaps it in. The previous big model is unloaded (24GB fits one). The resident gemma3-12b-vision (ttl 28800) stays warm for everyday use.

instruction: What are the llama-swap settings for gemma3-12b-vision?
output: See llama-swap/models.yaml: cmd with -ngl 999, -c per model, -ub/-b, -np 1, --no-mmap, ttl 1800 (28800 for the resident vision model). IPEX SYCL: f16 KV, no flash-attn, no KV-quant. Vulkan binary for gpt-oss/Qwen3-VL/Omni.

instruction: A request for local-chat is slow on first call but fast after. Why?
input: First call for local-chat after idle.
output: Cold load: llama-swap loads the GGUF on demand (e.g. gpt-oss-20b ~15s warm, Qwen2.5-VL-7B ~32s load). After that the model is resident until ttl expires, so later calls are fast. The resident vision model (ttl 28800) avoids this for everyday use.

output: Client calls :4000 with model "qwen2.5-vl". LiteLLM maps it to openai/qwen2.5-vl-7b at http://127.0.0.1:9090/v1. llama-swap loads qwen2.5-vl-7b on demand (only one big model fits in 24GB), serves it, and unloads after ttl.

instruction: How do you switch the resident model to qwen2.5-vl-7b?
output: Send a request naming qwen2.5-vl-7b (via its LiteLLM alias) to :4000; llama-swap hot-swaps it in. The previous big model is unloaded (24GB fits one). The resident gemma3-12b-vision (ttl 28800) stays warm for everyday use.

instruction: What are the llama-swap settings for qwen2.5-vl-7b?
output: See llama-swap/models.yaml: cmd with -ngl 999, -c per model, -ub/-b, -np 1, --no-mmap, ttl 1800 (28800 for the resident vision model). IPEX SYCL: f16 KV, no flash-attn, no KV-quant. Vulkan binary for gpt-oss/Qwen3-VL/Omni.

instruction: A request for qwen2.5-vl is slow on first call but fast after. Why?
input: First call for qwen2.5-vl after idle.
output: Cold load: llama-swap loads the GGUF on demand (e.g. gpt-oss-20b ~15s warm, Qwen2.5-VL-7B ~32s load). After that the model is resident until ttl expires, so later calls are fast. The resident vision model (ttl 28800) avoids this for everyday use.

instruction: Plan adding a new model to the Arc stack. What are the risks and mitigations?

output: 1) Run the 120 held-out tasks against stock Qwen3.8-27B (baseline). 2) Run the same set against sentinel-arc-27b-v1. 3) Score with the rubric (masking leak = auto-fail). 4) Check no coding regression, >=15 tok/s at 8k ctx. 5) Ship only if task success beats stock by >=10%. Risks: OOM at large ctx (mitigate: small -ub, vram-budget), session-0 CPU fallback (mitigate: interactive session), bad config (mitigate: SCP + ASCII + restart + curl verify), training on held-out data (mitigate: never train on eval/).

instruction: Drill 1: is gemma3-12b-max (6.8GB) the right model for a 131072-token coding task, or is local-coding better?

output: Remove the literal value, replace it with a ${ENV_VAR} reference, rotate the exposed key, and check history/logs for copies. Never commit a literal key.
